newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan rate rise could hurt corporate prospects-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan rate rise could hurt corporate prospects-MOF.

text.p: Japan's economy remains on a recovery trend, but the Bank of Japan may have to be cautious about raising the official discount rate as an increase in interest rates may hurt the business prospects of corporations, a senior Finance Ministry official told Reuters on Friday.

The official said he is not worried about the future course of the economy as corporate profits are improving, the business mood is brightening and capital spending is showing signs of improving in the future.

Regarding speculation among some operators in financial markets that the BOJ will raise the discount rate soon, the official said the benefits from having a low interest rate policy outweighed the disadvantages.

"If the BOJ were to tighten its credit policy, this would dampen the business mood which is currently brightening. An increase in the discount rate carries such risk and therefore the BOJ may have to be cautious about raising it," he said.
The BOJ has kept the discount rate at a historically low level of 0.5 percent since September 1995 to support the economy.
BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita has repeatedly said the BOJ's monetary policy is currently aimed at ensuring a firm economic recovery.
